question: In Grade 12 Technical Sciences, how is **'Hooke's Law'** defined?
correct_answer: Within the limit of proportionality, the extension produced in an elastic material is directly proportional to the applied deforming force.
wrong_answers_pool: Stress is inversely proportional to strain in all plastic materials
The pressure applied to an enclosed fluid decreases with distance
The rate of change of momentum is proportional to the applied force
The strain of a material equals its cross-sectional area squared
All liquids compress uniformly when subjected to mechanical shock
Force equals mass times acceleration in hydraulic systems
explanation: Hooke's Law states: Within the limit of proportionality, extension is directly proportional to the applied force: F = k * Δx.

question: In Grade 12 Technical Sciences, how is **'Elasticity'** defined?
correct_answer: The property of a material by virtue of which it regains its original shape and size when the deforming force is removed.
wrong_answers_pool: The tendency of a material to deform permanently under small loads
The internal friction between adjacent layers of a flowing liquid
The property of fracturing suddenly without any plastic deformation
The resistance of a solid metal to scratching by diamond indenters
The ability of a metal to conduct heat and electricity rapidly
The property of liquids transmitting pressure in one direction
explanation: Elasticity is the physical ability of a body to return to its original dimensions after the external deforming force ceases.

question: In Grade 12 Technical Sciences, how is **'Plasticity (Plastic Deformation)'** defined?
correct_answer: The property of a material by virtue of which it undergoes permanent deformation and does NOT regain its original shape and size after the deforming force is removed.
wrong_answers_pool: The ability to return perfectly to original dimensions after stretching
The resistance of engine oil to flow at high temperatures
The multiplication of force in closed hydraulic cylinders
The property of glowing white hot when carrying heavy currents
The ability to resist chemical corrosion in acidic environments
The state of matter where liquids solidify under high pressure
explanation: Plastic deformation is permanent deformation; when the stress exceeds the elastic limit, the material remains permanently stretched or distorted.

question: In Grade 12 Technical Sciences, how is **'Stress (Tensile / Compressive Stress, σ)'** defined?
correct_answer: The internal restoring force per unit cross-sectional area of a material (σ = F / A, measured in pascals or N·m⁻²).
wrong_answers_pool: The ratio of change in length to original length of a wire
The maximum force a hydraulic jack can exert on a vehicle
The speed at which a crack propagates through brittle glass
The spring constant multiplied by the square of extension
The frictional drag between fluid molecules in a pipe
The force applied divided by the volume of the material
explanation: Stress is defined as the internal restoring force per unit cross-sectional area: σ = F / A (units: N·m⁻² or Pa).

tags.learning_outcome: Define Stress (Tensile / Compressive Stress, σ)

question: In Grade 12 Technical Sciences, how is **'Strain (Tensile / Compressive Strain, ε)'** defined?
correct_answer: The fractional change in length of a material, calculated as the ratio of change in length (extension) to original length (ε = ΔL / L_0, a dimensionless ratio).
wrong_answers_pool: The internal force divided by cross-sectional area of a rod
The slope of a pressure versus volume hydraulic graph
The percentage increase in liquid viscosity per degree Celsius
The spring stiffness constant expressed in newtons per meter
The energy dissipated as heat during irreversible fracture
The mechanical advantage of a hydraulic slave piston
explanation: Strain is the ratio of change in length to original length: ε = ΔL / L_0. Because it is length divided by length, strain has no units.

tags.subject: Technical Sciences
tags.learning_outcome: Define Strain (Tensile / Compressive Strain, ε)

question: In Grade 12 Technical Sciences, how is **'Modulus of Elasticity (Young's Modulus, K or E)'** defined?
correct_answer: The ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain within the limit of proportionality of a material (K = σ / ε, measured in pascals or N·m⁻²).
wrong_answers_pool: The maximum load a cable can support before snapping completely
The product of stress multiplied by strain in a tensile test
The ratio of force applied to extension in a compression spring
The density of an incompressible fluid inside a brake master cylinder
The work done in stretching an elastic cord to twice its length
The rate of flow of engine lubricant through an orifice
explanation: Young's Modulus (Modulus of Elasticity) measures the stiffness of a solid material and is defined as K = stress / strain = σ / ε.

tags.subject: Technical Sciences
tags.learning_outcome: Define Modulus of Elasticity (Young's Modulus, K or E)

question: In Grade 12 Technical Sciences, how is **'Pascal's Principle'** defined?
correct_answer: Pressure exerted on an enclosed, incompressible liquid is transmitted equally and undiminished in all directions throughout the liquid.
wrong_answers_pool: Fluid speed increases as pipe diameter decreases in flow lines
The buoyant force on an object equals the weight of fluid displaced
Viscosity of a lubricant increases as temperature increases
The pressure in a fluid drops to zero at the bottom of a container
Force is multiplied only when fluids are compressed into gases
Liquids expand to fill the entire volume of their container
explanation: Pascal's Principle states that pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted undiminished to every portion of the fluid and the walls of the vessel.

tags.learning_outcome: Define Pascal's Principle

question: In Grade 12 Technical Sciences, how is **'Viscosity'** defined?
correct_answer: The property of a fluid that determines its internal resistance to flow (internal fluid friction between adjacent sliding liquid layers).
wrong_answers_pool: The ability of a liquid to be compressed into a smaller volume
The maximum pressure a fluid can transmit in a hydraulic press
The rate at which a liquid evaporates at atmospheric pressure
The ratio of liquid density compared to the density of pure water
The property of a liquid to stick to the container glass walls
The mechanical force exerted by a piston on brake fluid
explanation: Viscosity is fluid friction: the measure of a fluid's internal resistance to gradual deformation by shear or flow.

question: On an engineering stress-strain graph, what is the meaning of: **'Limit of Proportionality'**?
correct_answer: The point on a stress-strain curve up to which stress is directly proportional to strain (Hooke's law is obeyed).
wrong_answers_pool: The point where the material breaks into two separate pieces
The point where the material begins to flow like a liquid
The point of maximum stress the material can endure
The point where permanent deformation first becomes zero
The point where Young's modulus drops to zero
The point where the material becomes completely rigid
explanation: Limit of Proportionality is defined as: The point on a stress-strain curve up to which stress is directly proportional to strain (Hooke's law is obeyed)..

question: On an engineering stress-strain graph, what is the meaning of: **'Elastic Limit'**?
correct_answer: The maximum stress a material can withstand without undergoing permanent plastic deformation upon unloading.
wrong_answers_pool: The stress at which a material fractures instantly
The region where Hooke's law ceases to be linear
The minimum force required to insert a rivet
The point where a ductile metal converts into cast iron
The point of maximum cross-sectional necking
The stress required to compress hydraulic fluid
explanation: Elastic Limit is defined as: The maximum stress a material can withstand without undergoing permanent plastic deformation upon unloading..

question: On an engineering stress-strain graph, what is the meaning of: **'Yield Point'**?
correct_answer: The point at which a material begins to deform plastically with little or no increase in the applied load.
wrong_answers_pool: The exact point where the material regains its original shape

The point of ultimate tensile fracture
The point where viscosity becomes infinite

The point where mechanical advantage equals unity
explanation: Yield Point is defined as: The point at which a material begins to deform plastically with little or no increase in the applied load..

question: On an engineering stress-strain graph, what is the meaning of: **'Ultimate Tensile Stress (UTS)'**?
correct_answer: The maximum tensile stress that a material can withstand before necking occurs and it ultimately fractures.

question: Effect of increasing temperature on the viscosity of a liquid (such as engine motor oil)
correct_answer: The viscosity DECREASES, because thermal energy increases molecular kinetic energy and weakens the intermolecular cohesive forces between liquid layers.
wrong_answers_pool: The viscosity INCREASES, because liquid molecules collide more frequently.
The viscosity remains completely constant regardless of temperature.
The liquid converts into a solid under any temperature increase.
The liquid loses all ability to lubricate metallic gears.
The density of the liquid increases while viscosity doubles.
The fluid friction increases by 100% per 10 °C rise.
explanation: The viscosity DECREASES, because thermal energy increases molecular kinetic energy and weakens the intermolecular cohesive forces between liquid layers.

tags.subject: Technical Sciences
tags.learning_outcome: Understand viscosity and lubrication factors

question: Effect of decreasing temperature on the viscosity of a liquid
correct_answer: The viscosity INCREASES (the liquid becomes thicker and more sluggish to flow), because lower thermal energy strengthens intermolecular cohesive forces.
wrong_answers_pool: The viscosity decreases, making the liquid flow much faster.
The viscosity remains unchanged because volume is conserved.
The liquid boils immediately into high-pressure vapor.
The fluid friction drops to zero like a superfluid.
The liquid stops transmitting pressure in hydraulic pipes.
The mechanical advantage of hydraulic jacks drops to zero.
explanation: The viscosity INCREASES (the liquid becomes thicker and more sluggish to flow), because lower thermal energy strengthens intermolecular cohesive forces.

tags.subject: Technical Sciences
tags.learning_outcome: Understand viscosity and lubrication factors

question: Meaning of a multi-grade motor oil rating such as SAE 15W-40 in automotive engineering
correct_answer: The '15W' indicates low-temperature viscosity for easy winter cold engine starting, while '40' indicates high-temperature viscosity retention for engine protection at 100 °C.
wrong_answers_pool: The oil can only be used for 15 weeks before degrading in 40 °C heat.
The oil contains 15% water and 40% synthetic detergent additives.
The oil operates at 15 kW power up to 40 000 km distance.
The oil has a density of 15 kg/m³ and boiling point of 40 °C.
The oil provides 15 bars of pressure at 40 rpm engine speed.
The oil is designed exclusively for 15-year-old motor vehicles.
explanation: The '15W' indicates low-temperature viscosity for easy winter cold engine starting, while '40' indicates high-temperature viscosity retention for engine protection at 100 °C.

tags.subject: Technical Sciences
tags.learning_outcome: Understand viscosity and lubrication factors

question: Function of an engine lubricant / hydraulic fluid
correct_answer: To reduce friction and wear between moving metal surfaces, dissipate heat, prevent rust/corrosion, and transmit hydraulic force effectively.
wrong_answers_pool: To increase the tensile strength of the engine cylinder block
To combust inside the spark plug gap to provide horsepower
To solidify into a rigid plastic seal inside the crankshaft
To react chemically with steel to dissolve iron oxides permanently
To convert mechanical work into electrical potential energy
To stop all fluid flow through the oil filter completely
explanation: To reduce friction and wear between moving metal surfaces, dissipate heat, prevent rust/corrosion, and transmit hydraulic force effectively.

tags.subject: Technical Sciences
tags.learning_outcome: Understand viscosity and lubrication factors

question: Why are liquids (such as hydraulic mineral oil) used in hydraulic systems rather than gases (such as air)?
correct_answer: Liquids are virtually incompressible, allowing applied force and pressure to be transmitted instantaneously and efficiently without volume loss, whereas gases compress significantly before moving the load.
wrong_answers_pool: Liquids have zero density compared to atmospheric air.
Liquids create negative pressure that pulls pistons inward.
Gases react chemically with steel pistons to produce water.
Liquids eliminate the need for any mechanical seals or O-rings.
Gases cannot exert any pressure on solid boundaries.
Liquids freeze into solids when high pressure is applied.
explanation: Liquids are virtually incompressible, allowing applied force and pressure to be transmitted instantaneously and efficiently without volume loss, whereas gases compress significantly before moving the load.

tags.subject: Technical Sciences
tags.learning_outcome: Explain hydraulic principles and Pascal's Law

question: In a hydraulic lift, what happens to the pressure when a small force F1 is applied to small piston area A1?
correct_answer: The pressure P = F1 / A1 is transmitted equally throughout the entire fluid, exerting an upward force F2 = P × A2 on the larger piston area A2.
wrong_answers_pool: The pressure decreases proportionally to the ratio of piston areas.
The pressure increases only at the bottom corners of the reservoir.
The pressure drops to zero when the fluid touches the large piston.
The pressure on the large piston is doubled while force is halved.
The fluid creates electrical current that powers an electric motor.
The small piston moves down while the large piston moves down twice as far.
explanation: The pressure P = F1 / A1 is transmitted equally throughout the entire fluid, exerting an upward force F2 = P × A2 on the larger piston area A2.

tags.subject: Technical Sciences
tags.learning_outcome: Explain hydraulic principles and Pascal's Law

question: In an ideal hydraulic press, how does the mechanical advantage (MA) relate to the areas and diameters of the two pistons?
correct_answer: MA = F2 / F1 = A2 / A1 = (d2 / d1)², meaning force multiplication is directly proportional to the ratio of piston areas or the SQUARE of their diameters.
wrong_answers_pool: MA = A1 / A2 = d1 / d2 (inversely proportional to areas)
MA = d2 / d1 (linearly proportional to diameters)
MA = A2 × A1 (product of both piston surface areas)
MA = F1 / F2 (ratio of input force to output load)
MA is always equal to exactly 1.0 in any closed hydraulic system
MA = (d1 / d2)² (square of small diameter over large diameter)
explanation: MA = F2 / F1 = A2 / A1 = (d2 / d1)², meaning force multiplication is directly proportional to the ratio of piston areas or the SQUARE of their diameters.

tags.subject: Technical Sciences
tags.learning_outcome: Explain hydraulic principles and Pascal's Law

question: A sample of **High-carbon spring steel** (high stiffness and high tensile strength) is subjected to a tensile load of 10 N within its elastic limit. What happens to the specimen when the 10 N tensile load is completely removed?
correct_answer: It returns completely to its original dimensions (zero permanent plastic deformation) because the applied stress was below its elastic limit.
wrong_answers_pool: It remains permanently stretched and never returns to its original length.
It shatters immediately into microscopic powder upon load release.
Its cross-sectional area permanently doubles in size.
Its Young's modulus drops permanently to zero pascals.
Its mass decreases by 50% due to mechanical fatigue.
It converts into a high-viscosity liquid under zero load.
explanation: It returns completely to its original dimensions (zero permanent plastic deformation) because the applied stress was below its elastic limit.

tags.subject: Technical Sciences
tags.learning_outcome: Explain elastic behavior of High-carbon spring steel

question: A helical spring obeys Hooke's law up to a proportional limit of 20 N. When a load of 10 N is suspended, its extension is measured. If the suspended load is DOUBLED to 20 N, what happens to the extension?
correct_answer: The extension DOUBLES, because within the limit of proportionality, extension is directly proportional to applied force (F ∝ Δx).
wrong_answers_pool: The extension is halved because of spring stiffness.
The extension quadruples because force is squared.
The spring snaps instantly into two pieces.
The spring contracts and becomes shorter than its rest length.
explanation: The extension DOUBLES, because within the limit of proportionality, extension is directly proportional to applied force (F ∝ Δx).

tags.subject: Technical Sciences
tags.learning_outcome: Apply Hooke's law direct proportionality

explanation: Hooke's Law: F = k × Δx. Convert extension: 15.0 cm = 0.150 m. F = 2000 N·m⁻¹ × 0.150 m = 300.0 N.

tags.subject: Technical Sciences
tags.learning_outcome: Calculate deforming force from spring constant
